title: Time-windowed variant warmup + soft-enforce fallback policy for pinned model versions
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: When customers pin to a specific model version we need an automated, low-risk fallback policy that preserves latency SLOs and quality while making deprecation enforcement predictable. Existing fallback playbooks are all-or-nothing or purely priority-based; they can either cause noisy immediate shifts or long tail outages when a pinned variant deprecates or becomes degraded.

Proposal summary: Implement a time-windowed, warmup-first variant selection and a soft-enforce deprecation flow. Key ideas: (1) When a pinned version becomes unavailable or is exhibiting quality/latency regressions, route a percentage of traffic to warmup candidate variants (region-aware) with increasing weights over a configurable time window; (2) select candidate variants by a scored ranking that blends regional capacity, historical latency P95, inferred quality delta (from eval sets or runtime regressions), and storage/compatibility hints; (3) when deprecation thresholds are met, emit staged enforcement alerts to customers and only fully evict pin after N windows or a forced admin action.

Goals: reduce user-facing errors during deprecations, limit large cold-start-induced latency spikes, give customers a predictable, gradual transition path, and enable console visibility for each step.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can take a pinned request and split it into 0-100% traffic to N candidate variants over a configurable time window
Ranking function returns deterministic top-3 candidates per region using available signals (latency P95, error rate, quantization compatibility)
Console shows per-pin rollout progress and provides a one-click abort/accelerate control
Automated alerts sent to customer and SRE when soft-enforce threshold is hit; pin remains resolvable (returns 200) until hard-eviction after configured windows
End-to-end e2e test coverage and integration test with dedicated autoscaler simulated capacity drop
tasks: Spec policy DSL extensions for time-windowed weighted rollouts (design + examples)
Implement ranking component in routing service: signal ingestion + scoring function
Add warmup weight controller with safe-increment backoff and region-aware caps
Expose rollout state and controls in Console: progress bar, telemetry links, abort/force options
Add auditing/logging for fallback decisions and include `reason` tags for devtools/tracing
Write unit/integration tests and run chaos test (simulate region outage + quantized model miss)
design_notes: Scoring: score = w1*(1 - normalized_latency_p95) + w2*(1 - error_rate) + w3*(1 - quality_regression_score) + w4*compatibility_bonus. Weights adjustable per-customer tier.
Warmup schedule: default 5-minute window with exponential increments: 5%, 15%, 40%, 70%, 100% each minute. Configurable per pin and per region.
Compatibility hints: variant metadata includes tokenization match, kv-cache layout compatibility, and quantization profile tags. Incompatible variants get a hard penalty.

Deprecation policy: soft-enforce emits WARN at first threshold (e.g., 2 windows of P95>2x baseline OR error_rate>5%), then escalates to NOTIFY and finally to HARD-EVICT after 6 windows unless customer acknowledges.
Telemetry: attach rollup metrics (per-pin p50/p95, dropped requests, fallback_rate) and annotate traces with fallback.reason and fallback.window_id
implementation_notes: Add new DB table `pin_rollouts` with flat columns: pin_key, window_id, candidate_list (comma-separated), weights (comma-separated), start_ts, end_ts, state
Prefer stateless routing with rollout controller emitting signed rollout tokens that can be validated at the model-proxy level
Backfill variant metadata from model-catalog ingestion pipeline; ensure nightly job tags new uploads with compatibility footprints
Integrate with existing fallback ledger (ENG-58321) to reuse auditing hooks
Aim for incremental launch: feature-flag the warmup controller and enable per-organization opt-in
policy_example: policy: { scope: pin, trigger: deprecation_or_unavailable, strategy: time_windowed_warmup, window_minutes: 5, steps: ["5%", "15%", "40%", "70%", "100%" ], candidate_selector: { top_k: 3, score_weights: {latency:0.4, error:0.3, quality:0.2, compat:0.1}, region_sensitive: true }, alerts: { soft_warn: 2, hard_evict: 6 } }
tests_and_qa: Unit tests for ranking: synthetic signals to verify weighting behaves as expected
Integration test: simulate primary variant crash in us-west, verify warmup schedule routes incrementally and p95 stability
Chaos test: throttle model cache hit-rate to validate fallbacks avoid large latency blips
Load test: 10k concurrent requests for pinned routes during rollout windows to ensure router maintains throughput
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature flag + internal dogfood on staging (selected customers opt-in)
Week 2: limited production rollout to 5% of pinned traffic on selective orgs
Week 3: enable console controls and SRE alerting for all orgs; monitor for regressions
Week 4: GA with documentation and SDK examples
rollback_plan: Abort rollout: console button triggers immediate reweight to 0% for candidates and routes 100% back to original pin (if available)
If pin is unavailable, re-route to admin-configured emergency fallback variant and notify SRE
If systemic issue, flip global feature-flag to disable warmup controller and revert to current fallback behavior
